page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with a dedicated AMD EPYC 9354P processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.25 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a high resource density of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier PassMark memory scores and strong read/write bandwidth across both small and large blocks. For specialized workloads, the server achieves strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and redis SET operations, alongside top-tier LLM inference speeds for text generation using a medium 7B model.

The bare metal architecture provides dedicated hardware resources without hypervisor overhead, offering high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and compute-heavy deployments. The high memory-to-core ratio makes this server well-suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, and memory-bound data processing. Additionally, the strong CPU performance and advanced vector instruction support make it highly capable for multi-threaded compilation, web serving, and local LLM inference tasks.
